title: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion pumped by spatiotemporal structured light
abstract: Here we investigate the all-optical control of spectral correlations in spontaneous parametric down-conversion. We show that when photon pairs are projected onto high-order spatial modes, the spatial structure of the pump field defines the phase-matching function of the nonlinear interaction. Thus, by structuring the pump field in both space and spectrum, the biphoton spectral correlations are fully controlled.Considering a standard periodically-poled crystal as the nonlinear medium, we show that the Gouy phase matching method proposed here can generate both spectrally uncorrelated and high-dimensional spectrally entangled photon pairs, similarly to what is achieved with aperiodically-poled crystals. Furthermore, we show that our method can generate a wider class of quantum states if the pump field is a spatiotemporal wavepacket, that is, if its spatial and spectral structures are correlated.
summary: The paper presents a method to precisely control the spectral correlations of entangled photon pairs generated via SPDC using structured light pumps. By exploiting the Gouy phase mismatch, the authors show that structuring the pump in both space and spectrum allows for 'field-programmable' generation of complex quantum states. This offers a powerful alternative to traditional crystal engineering for advanced quantum source development.
main_problem: The research aims to achieve all-optical control over the spectral correlations of photon pairs generated via Spontaneous Parametric Down-Conversion (SPDC). This is accomplished by structuring the pump beam in both spatial and spectral domains.
main_result: By utilizing Gouy phase matching with spatiotemporally structured light, the authors demonstrate full control over biphoton spectral correlations, enabling the generation of complex quantum states inaccessible through traditional crystal engineering methods.
method: The method involves modeling SPDC using mode expansions (e.g., Hermite-Gaussian basis) and deriving the joint spectral amplitude (JSA) dependence on the pump field's spatiotemporal structure via the Gouy phase mismatch.
model_or_system: The physical system is SPDC in a nonlinear medium, modeled by an interaction Hamiltonian. The control mechanism relies on structuring the pump beam using its spatial and temporal wavepacket properties to dictate the effective phase-matching function.
key_observables: Mode-dependent joint spectral amplitude (mJSA), fidelity of the effective nonlinear susceptibility ($\chi_{	ext{eff}}$) matching target Hermite-Gaussian structures, and spectral purity ($P$).
important_parameters: The Gouy phase mismatch term $\Delta \phi_G(z)$ is crucial; control is achieved by structuring the pump field in space (spatial modes) and spectrum (temporal wavepackets).
main_assumptions: Approximations include using the standard SPDC regime (low pair generation probability) and assuming linear dispersion.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate conceptual setups with structured pumps, optimization results showing high fidelity of $\chi_{	ext{eff}}$ matching HG targets, and examples of generated JSAs using Laguerre-Gaussian modes in a rotated spectral basis.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by relating the mJSA to the pump field structure via Gouy phase matching. It then demonstrates this control capability by generating specific quantum states (separable vs. entangled) and compares it favorably against previous methods like those using Aperiodically Poled Crystals.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics, specifically in the area of photon source engineering. The concept of 'field-programmable' sources that bypass complex crystal fabrication techniques by manipulating the pump beam is a major theoretical advance for generating high-dimensional entangled states.
